question_text: Find the angle between the curves xy = 2 and x² + 4y = 0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you reduce the two equations to one, what cubic you get, and what formula gives the angle.

steps.label: Find the point of intersection
steps.margin_note: Two marks. From xy = 2 write y = 2/x and substitute. The result is a cubic, x³ + 8 = 0, which has exactly one real root — so there is only one point to work at.
lines: Multiply by x:  x³ + 8 = 0  ⇒  x³ = −8  ⇒  x = −2
(x³ + 8 = (x + 2)(x² − 2x + 4), and x² − 2x + 4 has no real root.)
∴ the curves meet only at P(−2, −1).

recall.must_convey: That y = 2/x substituted into x² + 4y = 0 gives x³ + 8 = 0, so x = −2 and the point is (−2, −1).

steps.why: The angle between two curves is the angle between their tangents at a shared point, so the point comes first. Substituting y = 2/x is the shorter route here because y appears to the first power in the second curve.
common_mistakes: Reading x³ = −8 as x = 2 and losing the sign.
Taking three roots from the cubic without checking that two of them are not real.
Getting y = −2 and x = −1 by putting the coordinates in the wrong order.
steps.memory_tip: A rectangular hyperbola xy = c always gives y = c/x. Substituting that and clearing the x in the denominator raises the degree; here it gives a cubic.

steps.label: Find both slopes there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The first curve is a product, so differentiating xy needs the product rule. Both coordinates are negative here, so watch every sign.
lines: From (i):  xy = 2. Differentiate using the product rule:

steps.why: xy is a product of two functions of x, so its derivative is y + x·dy/dx. Treating x and y as if they multiplied to a single term is the usual error and gives the wrong slope.
common_mistakes: Differentiating xy as dy/dx without the product rule.
Sign slip in −(−1)/(−2), giving +1/2 instead of −1/2.
Differentiating 4y as 4 with no dy/dx factor.
steps.memory_tip: For xy = c the slope is always −y/x, which is the product rule already done once.

steps.label: Apply the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The denominator 1 + m₁m₂ works out to 1/2, so the fraction is (−3/2) ÷ (1/2) = −3, and the modulus makes it 3.

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| = 3, so θ = Tan⁻¹3.

steps.why: There is only one point of intersection, so there is only one angle to report. The modulus keeps the acute angle, which is the standard answer for the angle between two curves.
common_mistakes: Writing 1 − m₁m₂ in the denominator instead of 1 + m₁m₂.
Stopping at tanθ = 3 without stating the angle.
steps.memory_tip: Difference on top, one plus the product underneath, modulus around the whole fraction.

insider_note: Substituting gives x³ = −8, which has ONE real root, x = −2 — the quadratic factor has no real roots. So there is a single point of intersection.
